title: Sheriff Cuellar Goes Public: His Own Page Posted the 'Remove My Name' Message
excerpt: The 'remove my name' message is no longer just a screenshot — Sheriff Martin Cuellar's own Facebook page posted it. And a second sheriff is reportedly pushing back.
content:
The message at the center of this week's endorsement scandal is no longer just a screenshot. On Monday afternoon, the public Facebook page operating under Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar's name published the image itself, with a two-word caption: "Read below." The screenshot shows a text message sent at 11:43 a.m. Monday to Texas Tribune reporter Brandon Waltens, whose post that morning had announced the endorsements. The message reads: "Please remove my name from this endorsement for the governor. abbott. This is sheriff martin Cuellar. The governor endorsed tano my brother's opponent. Thank you."

That changes the record. When Webb Watch 956 first reported the removal early Tuesday, the message was an unattributed screenshot racing across Laredo social media and its authenticity was unconfirmed. A public post from the sheriff's own page is a different thing: the sheriff's side has put the removal request on the record itself. The post was shared the same day by Laredo outlets including 24/7 Laredo and Vive Laredo.

A second sheriff is reportedly pushing back

The Rio Grande Current reported Tuesday that at least two of the 12 sheriffs on Gov. Greg Abbott's original list are now pushing back, under the headline "Abbott's Sheriff Endorsements Start Unraveling" — and asked the question the campaign has not answered: did all 12 sheriffs actually endorse him? The Current's reporting available to Webb Watch 956 does not name the second sheriff, and we have not independently confirmed a second withdrawal. What is documented: the campaign's endorsement page, last updated at 11:45 a.m. Monday, now lists 11 sheriffs — and neither the campaign nor the sheriff's office has publicly explained the change.

Where the list stands

The 11 sheriffs the campaign now lists are Ronnie Dodson (Brewster County), Urbino "Benny" Martinez (Brooks), Oscar E. Carillo (Culberson), Chris Castaneda (Dimmit), Romeo Ramirez (Duval), Erasmo "Kiko" Alarcon Jr. (Jim Hogg), Ramon Salinas III (Kenedy), Danny Dominguez (Presidio), Joe Frank Martinez (Val Verde), Ramon Montes (Zapata) and Eusevio Salinas (Zavala). The campaign says 103 Texas sheriffs have endorsed Abbott overall. Cuellar's name is the only one that disappeared.

The case behind the sheriff

Cuellar, the brother of U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar of Laredo, was named in a five-count federal indictment returned in November 2025. Prosecutors allege that he and two former assistant chiefs used sheriff's office staff and resources to run a for-profit, COVID-era disinfecting company, Disinfect Pro Master. Cuellar has pleaded not guilty and says he is innocent and will fight the charges. One former assistant chief, Ricardo Rodriguez, has pleaded guilty. The sheriff's trial, once set for this month, was pushed to February 2027. Separately, a removal petition filed by former Laredo council member Alfonso "Poncho" Casso asks a court to suspend and remove him from office; Cuellar has denied those allegations in court filings.

What we still don't know

Three questions remain open: whether Cuellar ever agreed to endorse Abbott in the first place; why the campaign listed an indicted sheriff on a law-and-order rollout and then removed him within hours on the first day of early voting, without a word of explanation; and whether a second sheriff is in fact disputing the endorsement, as reported. As of publication, neither the Abbott campaign nor the sheriff's office has publicly answered any of them. Early voting runs through October 30. Election Day is November 3.

Sources: Sheriff Martin Cuellar Facebook page post, Oct. 19, 2026; The Rio Grande Current, "Abbott's Sheriff Endorsements Start Unraveling," Oct. 20, 2026; Texas Gazette, "Abbott Touts Backing From Democratic Border Sheriffs as Voting Opens," Oct. 19-20, 2026; The Texas Voice, "Border-Area Democrat Sheriffs Endorse Abbott," Oct. 20, 2026; KGNS reporting on the Martin Cuellar indictment, via Texas Gazette; San Antonio Current, reporting on the removal petition.

— Walter Webb & Willa Webb, News Anchors, Webb Watch 956
